# Phase 01.1 Plan 12: Re-skin the Tablet Route Group Summary

The enrolment landing, the enable-staff-mode flow, the unlock screen and the PIN pad now render in the
Cena design system, with the idle-relock timer and the PIN and unenrol behaviours held byte-identical
under diff gates — and with the group's five glyph call sites moved onto the `Icon` wrapper.

## What Was Built

**The three pages (Task 1).** One shell now runs across the route group: the page field is the
secondary 30% surface, and anything a hand touches sits on paper — the name tiles, the PIN keys, the
enrolment form, the unlock button cluster. A state with nothing to touch (the zero-staff message)
renders as type on the field and takes no paper panel, because a panel around a sentence frames
nothing. Page titles moved out of `Card` and onto the field, which is what promotes them from the
Heading role a `CardTitle` carries to the Display role in serif that a page title takes. Margins are
32px and section gaps 24px, read from the named spacing scale rather than written as raw steps.

**The PIN pad (Task 2).** Both glyphs route through `Icon` at the 1.75 stroke. Digits take
`--font-mono`. The dot indicators stay display-only at 12px with 8px gaps, exempt from the 44px floor
rather than grown to satisfy a rule they are not subject to. The accent reaches this screen only as a
momentary pressed state, carried by all twelve keys alike through one shared class constant so a press
reads the same wherever it lands.

**The four action components (Task 3).** Three spinner sites moved to `Icon`. The enrolment form took
the 8 / 16 / 24 form rhythm and dropped its local `h-11` override, because the input primitive owns the
floor now and a second place to decide it is a second place for it to drift. "Enable staff mode" stays
the one accent-filled control on its screen.

## The 44px Floor: Measured, Not Assumed

The orchestrator's instruction was to treat any sub-44px measurement here as a real defect, so every
value below was read out of the **compiled** stylesheet rather than inferred from the class name.
`--spacing` resolves to `0.25rem`, so:

| Control | Class | Compiled |
|---|---|---|
| Name tile | `min-h-24 min-w-24` | 96 × 96 |
| PIN key (all 12) | `min-h-16 min-w-16` | 64 × 64 |
| Back / retry buttons | `min-h-12` | 48 |
| Input, native select, owner-access link | `h-11` / `min-h-11` | 44 |
| PIN dot indicator | `size-3` | 12 — **display-only, exempt by contract** |
| Error row | `min-h-5` | 20 — **a reserved text line, not a control** |

Nothing regressed. Nothing in this group needed raising because it was already generous, with one
exception recorded below.

## Deviations from Plan

### Auto-fixed Issues

**1. [Rule 2 — missing critical functionality] The owner-access link had no hit area at all**

- **Found during:** Task 1
- **Issue:** `/unlock` was reached from the PIN grid through bare underlined text with no height,
  padding or focus treatment. On a tablet used standing and one-handed, that is a control well below
  the 44px floor — and it is the only route an owner has out of the PIN grid without knowing the URL.
  It is a pre-existing gap rather than a migration regression, but the phase's floor is universal and
  the orchestrator's standing instruction was to treat a measurement below 44px as a real defect.
- **Fix:** raised to `min-h-11` with horizontal padding and the phase's focus ring. The painted text
  stays exactly as quiet as it was — the `link` button variant was deliberately *not* used, because it
  would paint this azure and make a discreet secondary route read as the screen's primary action,
  which is the opposite of what the component's own header asks for.
- **Files modified:** `app/(tablet)/page.tsx`
- **Commit:** 39a4b63

**2. [Rule 1 — bug] The unenrol hint rendered at a size outside all four type roles**

- **Found during:** Task 3
- **Issue:** `text-sm` on the hint under "Stop using this browser as a tablet". The system has exactly
  four size roles and `text-sm` is none of them, so this string was rendering at whatever Tailwind's
  stock value happens to be rather than at anything the contract names.
- **Fix:** moved to the Label role.
- **Files modified:** `app/(tablet)/components/UnenrollBrowserButton.tsx`
- **Commit:** b2188b2

### Deliberate non-changes

**`IdleRelock.tsx` has an empty diff, and that is the plan's own stated valid outcome.** The component
returns `null` — it renders no chrome to re-skin. Its timer duration, its four reset conditions and its
relock trigger are untouched, and the diff gate (`setTimeout|setInterval|clearTimeout|clearInterval|`
any 3+-digit literal) prints nothing because there is nothing to print. T-01.1-41 is closed by the file
not having been opened.

**No string moved.** `git diff lib/copy.ts` is empty across all three commits, closing T-01.1-42. Both
PIN error rows render unchanged, backoff seconds included.

**The unenrol path is untouched.** Its diff gate over `fetch|action|cookie` prints nothing, closing
T-01.1-43. It still clears locally and still does not revoke server-side.

## Coverage: the Glyph Migration

The tablet group is **5 of 5** migrated — `NameGridPinPad` (2), `EnableStaffModeForm`,
`ExitOwnerModeButton`, `UnenrollBrowserButton`. A scan that resolves each file's actual `lucide-react`
import list and looks for those names used as JSX elements returns **zero hits under `app/(tablet)/`**.

Nine files elsewhere in the repo still hold bare glyphs. **All nine belong to the three plans running
concurrently with this one** and none was touched:

| Owner | Files |
|---|---|
| 01.1-09 (auth) | `signup/page.tsx`, `login-form.tsx`, `password-reset-forms.tsx` |
| 01.1-10 (dashboard/venues) | `layout.tsx`, `venue-switcher-menu.tsx`, `components/venue-form.tsx` |
| 01.1-11 (staff) | `staff-provision-form.tsx`, `deactivate-staff-dialog.tsx`, `revoke-device-dialog.tsx` |

The eighteen-site migration is therefore complete *for this plan's share of it*; plan 01.1-14's
discipline test is the thing that will prove the repo-wide total once the wave merges.

## Findings for a Later Plan

**1. `01.1-UI-SPEC.md` contradicts itself on the mono family's size role.** § "Family axis" states the
mono family "renders at the Label or Body role, never at a size of its own"; § "Currency" states
"Prices render in `--font-mono` at the Heading role." Both cannot hold. This plan's `must_haves` names
the first form explicitly for PIN digits, so PIN digits took the Body role — the larger of the two
permitted. **A diner-phase agent implementing prices will hit the other side of this and should not
have to re-derive the answer.** Worth settling in 01.1-13 or 01.1-14.

**2. Eight user-visible strings in the tablet group have no copy-deck row.** `"Manage this venue"`,
`"Hi, {name}"`, `"You're signed in on this tablet."`, `"Currently signed in: {name}"`, `"Setting up…"`,
`"Locking…"`, `"Un-enrolling…"`, `"Choose a venue"`, plus the `"Delete last digit"` accessible label.
`lib/copy.ts`'s house rule is that a user-visible string with no contract row signals the design has no
screen for that state. This plan could not fix them: its acceptance criteria require an empty
`lib/copy.ts` diff and forbid changing any string, and three sibling agents hold that file's
neighbourhood this wave. Recorded, not fixed.

**3. The universal base-layer rule in `app/globals.css` still sets its outline colour at half opacity**
while all 19 primitives ship the contract's 30%. It is the fallback focus treatment for any element
that does not declare its own, so it is a second focus treatment surviving in the repo. Outside this
plan's `files_modified`; flagging for whoever owns `globals.css` next.

## Threat Flags

None. This plan added no network endpoint, no auth path, no file access and no schema change. The four
threats in its register (T-01.1-41 through T-01.1-44) are all closed as recorded above.
